metadata.description: A GTM operating system in Notion, built by plugins rather than by a consultant. The databases are created once by setup and written to by the plugins that own them, and no plugin calls another.

plugins.name: setup
plugins.description: Creates the Notion databases the foundation plugins read and write, wires the relations between them, and writes the foundation's config. Nothing else in the marketplace creates a database, and nothing else writes the foundation's config. install explains the model before it asks anything, asks only the questions that are genuinely the user's to decide, and reads everything it created back out of Notion before calling itself done.

plugins.name: calendar
plugins.description: The GTM calendar: what is happening in market, and when. Shows what else is already aimed at the same people before it writes anything, asks how it went when a row is marked done, and answers what an audience is receiving for a window. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: process
plugins.description: The Process library: the living reference of how and why things are done. Finds current answers, audits stale or conflicting artifacts, and sweeps scoped documents, conversations, meetings, CRM activity, billing, and spend evidence for missing process knowledge. Proposes candidates one approval at a time. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: memos
plugins.description: Time-stamped communication, append-only. Writes one memo of any of seven types from free-form notes or explicitly scoped Slack and Gmail context, turns a meeting into a record of what it decided, assembles the recurring team update from Projects, Calendar, Memos and Tasks rather than from memory, and finds what was said about something and when, following corrections to the end of the chain. There is no update skill and there never will be: a correction is a new memo. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: projects
plugins.description: Runs a project from named problem to shipped release. Finds recurring problems in bounded internal, meeting, CRM, sales-engagement and support context, writes the case that one is worth fixing, works out what a project is and deliberately is not before it is built, creates the tasks and starts the work, tells the people affected what changed, and records what shipped when it closes. External connectors are read-only and Notion is the only write destination. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: software
plugins.description: The Software directory: what we use, who owns it, what we pay and when that comes round again, and what would break if it went away. Adds one tool in conversation after checking for a duplicate, changes the facts when they change without touching the freshness stamp, confirms a whole row is still true and stamps the date only on a real pass, reports which renewals are coming up ordered by consequence rather than by date ending with what it could not see, and backfills the directory from a folder of contracts and your own mailbox, one approval at a time, never filling a person, an importance, or the review stamp. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: import-leads
plugins.description: Imports lead lists into the CRM config names, HubSpot or Salesforce, one per install: mapped, deduped, matched to companies, on the memberships the org's grid names, verified by reading every write back, and written back to a Notion source. Every write sits behind one confirmation.
